reasoning_content:
Now let's build and start the stack. The full `docker compose up -d --build` would build backend, ml-service, dashboard, backup and start all. This may take a long time (ml-service downloads 4.6GB). The timeout is 600s per command. Let me first build images in the background or with long-running commands. Since each command has a 600s cap, I may need to run the build and let it continue.

Let me start with building all images. I'll run `docker compose build` which may exceed 600s. I could run it with nohup in background and poll.

Let's start the build in background, logging to a file.

Actually, given the guide says first start takes long due to 4.6GB download. Let me run the full `docker compose up -d --build` in background with nohup, then poll.

Let me do that.

action.command:
cd /workspace && nohup docker compose up -d --build > /tmp/compose_up.log 2>&1 &
echo "started pid $!"; sleep 5; tail -5 /tmp/compose_up.log

tool_call.name: terminal
tool_call.arguments: {"command": "cd /workspace && nohup docker compose up -d --build > /tmp/compose_up.log 2>&1 &\necho \"started pid $!\"; sleep 5; tail -5 /tmp/compose_up.log", "security_risk": "MEDIUM", "summary": "Start compose stack build in background"}
